q-95567.name: Question 1
q-95567.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=-2\operatorname{coth}⁡g,\,g=4x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=2{csch}^{2}\,g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=4.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =2{csch}^{2}⁡g\cdot 4 \\  & =8{csch}^{2}⁡g \\  & =8{csch}^{2}⁡4x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−2coth⁡4x.

a
 4xcsch2⁡4x
b
 −8sech2⁡4x
c
 8csch⁡4xcoth⁡4x
d
 8csch2⁡4x
e
 −2sech⁡4xcoth⁡4x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=−2coth⁡g,g=4x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=2csch2g,

and

dgdx=4.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=2csch2⁡g⋅4=8csch2⁡g=8csch2⁡4x.

q-95575.name: Question 2
q-95575.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=3{g}^{2},\,g=\operatorname{csch}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=6g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =6g(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =6(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-6{csch}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=xsech2⁡x.

a
 sech2⁡x(1−2xtanh2⁡x)
b
sech⁡x(1+2xtanh⁡x)
c
 sech2⁡x(1+2xcoth⁡x)
d
sech⁡x(1−2xcoth2⁡x)
e
sech2⁡x(1−2xtanh⁡x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=x and v(x)=sech2⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(x)′⋅sech2⁡x+x⋅(sech2⁡x)′=1⋅sech2⁡x+x⋅(2sech⁡x)⋅(−sec⁡xtanh⁡x)=sech2⁡x−2xsech2⁡xtanh⁡x=sech2⁡x(1−2xtanh⁡x)

q-95891.name: Question 4
q-95891.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡x$ and $v(x)={e}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot {e}^{x}-\operatorname{coth}⁡x\cdot {({e}^{x})}^{′}}{{({e}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-{csch}^{2}⁡x)\cdot {e}^{x}-\operatorname{coth}⁡x\cdot ({e}^{x})}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{x}({csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x)}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡2x$ and $v(x)=2x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
